## The mixture equation of state: gas pressure from gas concentrations (`TPX->V`, `VT->P`, `PV->T`) {#sec-ch03-eos}

### Summary

kintera stores a mixture of gases and condensates as one list of species, gases first and condensates after them.
The equation of state relates the pressure to the temperature and the molar concentrations of the gases only. The
condensates carry mass, energy and entropy, but no pressure, and their volume is not subtracted from the gas
volume. Every conversion between a temperature-pressure description and a concentration description goes through
this one relation.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Gas pressure from gas concentrations, @eq-ch03-eos-pressure; concentrations from mole fractions,
@eq-ch03-eos-conc.

**Data.** $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], concentrations $c_n$ [mol m$^{-3}$], mole fractions $x_n$ [-].

**Placement.** Inside `ThermoX.compute` and `ThermoY.compute`, and so inside every caller of them.

**Activation.** Always. $z_n = 1$ unless C++ code sets a compressibility function (`czh`); YAML and Python cannot.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact for $z_n = 1$; otherwise a Newton iteration to `ftol`.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Symbols of the notation table (@sec-appa): $c_n$, molar concentration [mol m$^{-3}$]; $x_n$, mole fraction among all species [-];
$x_{\mathrm g}$, sum of the gas mole fractions [-]; $z_n$, compressibility factor [-]; $N_{\mathrm g}$, number of gas
species. Local symbols: $n$, species index, gases $n < N_{\mathrm g}$ first, then condensates. Species $n = 0$ is the
first gas, which the code treats as the reference ("dry") species.

### Derivation

The gases share the whole volume and each obeys the ideal-gas law corrected by its compressibility factor. Summing
the partial pressures $p_n = z_n c_n \mathcal R T$ over the gases gives

$$
p = \mathcal R T \sum_{n < N_{\mathrm g}} z_n c_n .
$$ {#eq-ch03-eos-pressure}

@eq-ch03-eos-pressure is computed in `_temp_to_pres`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_temp_to_pres >}}), which sums over the first $N_{\mathrm g}$
entries only. With the default $z_n = 1$ it is Dalton's law for ideal gases.

To go from mole fractions to concentrations, let $c$ be the total molar concentration of all species, gas and
condensed, so that $c_n = x_n c$. The gas moles are the fraction $x_{\mathrm g} = \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} x_n$ of
the total. For $z_n = 1$, @eq-ch03-eos-pressure becomes

$$
\begin{aligned}
p &= \mathcal R T \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} x_n c = \mathcal R T\, x_{\mathrm g}\, c , \\
c &= \frac{p}{\mathcal R T x_{\mathrm g}} .
\end{aligned}
$$

Every species, gas or condensate, has $c_n = x_n c$ with this one total, so

$$
c_n = \frac{x_n\, p}{\mathcal R T x_{\mathrm g}} \quad \text{for every } n \text{, gas or condensate} .
$$ {#eq-ch03-eos-conc}

Only the gas sum $x_{\mathrm g}$ enters the denominator, because condensates occupy no volume and exert no pressure:
a mixture with condensates has a larger total concentration than its gas pressure alone suggests. The gas lines of
@eq-ch03-eos-conc are computed in `_xfrac_to_conc`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::_xfrac_to_conc >}}). At the pin the condensate lines are computed as
$c_m = c_0\, x_m / x_0$, from the first gas's concentration. That is the same number when $x_0 > 0$, $z_0 = 1$ and
$c_0$ is above the floor, but it is not finite when the first gas is absent ($x_0 = 0$): the defect D16.[^ch03-d16]
Its fix scales the condensates by the summed gas concentrations, $c_m = x_m \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} c_n / x_{\mathrm g}$.
For $z_n = 1$ that is @eq-ch03-eos-conc; for $z_n \ne 1$ it uses the corrected gas concentrations, which keeps
$c_m / \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} c_n = x_m / x_{\mathrm g}$, so the condensates keep their mole ratios to each other and
to the total gas.
<!-- equation-source: eq-ch03-eos-conc code differs at x_0 = 0 (D16) -->

When a compressibility function is set, the gas concentrations solve $z_n(T, c_n)\, c_n = c^{\mathrm{id}}_n$,
where $c^{\mathrm{id}}_n$ is @eq-ch03-eos-conc for that gas. Newton's method on
$f(c_n) = z_n c_n - c^{\mathrm{id}}_n$ with $f'(c_n) = z_n + c_n\, \partial z_n / \partial c_n$ gives the update

$$
c_n \leftarrow c_n + \frac{c^{\mathrm{id}}_n - z_n c_n}{z_n + c_n\, \partial z_n / \partial c_n} .
$$

At the pin the condensate line uses the $c_0$ the gas step returns, which is first floored at `gas_floor` and then
Newton-corrected for $z_0$. Writing $c_0 = c^{\mathrm{id}}_0 / z_0$ and $c_n = c^{\mathrm{id}}_n / z_n$ gives

$$
\frac{c_m}{c_n} = \frac{x_m}{x_n}\, \frac{z_n}{z_0} ,
$$

so the returned concentrations reproduce the input mole fractions, $c_m / c_n = x_m / x_n$, only when $z_0 = z_n = 1$
and $c^{\mathrm{id}}_0$ is above the floor. Otherwise mole fractions recomputed from the concentrations differ from
the input. The relation is exact for $z_n = 1$ (the first iterate already satisfies it). With $z_n \ne 1$ it is solved to the
relative tolerance `ftol`.

### Numerical method

The equation of state is evaluated pointwise in every cell; it has no stencil and no boundary values. Three
conversions use it:

1. `TPX->V` (`ThermoX`): mole fractions to concentrations by @eq-ch03-eos-conc. The gas concentrations are first
   floored at `gas_floor` (default $10^{-20}$ mol m$^{-3}$); then the Newton update above runs until the largest
   relative change is below `ftol` or `max_iter` iterations are spent.
2. `VT->P` (`ThermoY`): pressure from concentrations by @eq-ch03-eos-pressure, in one evaluation.
3. `PV->T` (`ThermoY`): temperature from pressure and concentrations. The starting guess is
   $T = p / (\mathcal R \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} c_n)$, exact for $z_n = 1$. The update is
   $T \leftarrow T - f / \sum_n \left[(c_{p,n} - c_{v,n})/\mathcal R\right] c_n$ with
   $f = T \sum_n z_n c_n - p/\mathcal R$, a damped Newton step that uses the heat-capacity difference, in units of
   $\mathcal R$ as `eval_cp_R` and `eval_cv_R` return it, as the slope. For an ideal gas the bracket is 1 and the
   slope is $\sum_n c_n$, the exact derivative of $f$.

The equation-of-state figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| mole fractions to concentrations | {{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::_xfrac_to_conc >}} | `_xfrac_to_conc` | always |
| pressure | {{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_temp_to_pres >}} | `_temp_to_pres` | always |
| temperature from pressure | {{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_pres_to_temp >}} | `_pres_to_temp` | always |
| compressibility factor | {{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_czh >}} | `eval_czh` | `czh` |
| its derivative | {{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_czh_ddC >}} | `eval_czh_ddC` | `czh_ddC` |

: Code map of the equation of state. {#tbl-ch03-eos-code}

Warnings a user can hit: `_xfrac_to_conc` and `_pres_to_temp` warn when `max_iter` is reached. On that warning
`_xfrac_to_conc` also writes the inputs to a file named `thermo_x_xfrac_to_conc_<time>.pt` in the working
directory (verified by reading `_xfrac_to_conc` at the pin); `_pres_to_temp` writes nothing.

The tolerances are read from `tests/test_thermo.cpp` at the pin. The `DeviceTest` cases run on CPU in float32 and
float64, and on CUDA when a GPU is present. No test sets a compressibility function, so the Newton branch of
`_xfrac_to_conc` and the damped Newton of `_pres_to_temp` with $z_n \ne 1$ have missing evidence.

The derivation is checked by `check_ch3_eos.py`, on a card with one vapour and its condensate:[^ch03-eos-check]

- `(c1)`: for a gas-only state and a cloudy state with $x_0 = 0.5$, $\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} c_n \mathcal R T = p$ and
  the condensate concentration equals $x_m p / (\mathcal R T x_{\mathrm g})$, both exactly (0 against $10^{-13}$).
- `(c2)`: the same cloudy composition without species 0: the gas sum is still exact, and the condensate line
  returns `inf` at the pin instead of 4.454533 mol m$^{-3}$, EXPECTED-FAIL (D16).

`check_ch3_species_functions.py`, line `1c`, confirms the same two relations on `tests/jupiter.yaml` with a cloud
present (gas sum 1.5e-16, $c_m/c_n = x_m/x_n$ to 2.2e-16).

### Limits

Condensate volume is neglected: the gas occupies the whole volume. At the pin the condensate concentrations are
$c_0 x_m / x_0$ instead of @eq-ch03-eos-conc. With $x_0 = 0$, $c_0$ is floored to `gas_floor` ($10^{-20}$ mol
m$^{-3}$), and every condensate with $x_m > 0$ gets $c_m = 10^{-20} x_m / 0 = +\infty$ in IEEE arithmetic, while
$x_m = 0$ gives NaN. The check measures it: line `(c2)` returns `inf` for the cloud of a pure vapour with its
condensate (D16).[^ch03-d16] More generally, any $x_0$ with $c^{\mathrm{id}}_0 < 10^{-20}$ mol m$^{-3}$ inflates the
condensate concentrations by the floor. The non-ideal branches are untested.

The compressibility hooks are reachable from C++ only. No YAML key sets `czh` or `czh_ddC`; `populate_thermo`
({{< code src/species.cpp populate_thermo >}}), run by every `ThermoX` and `ThermoY` constructor, pads them with
empty names, and the Python bindings expose only `cref_R`, `uref_R` and `sref_R`
of the species options (verified by reading both at the pin), so a YAML or Python user always has $z_n = 1$.
Where a C++ caller does set $z_n \ne 1$, only the conversions of this section use it: the saturation conditions of
@sec-ch04 keep the ideal-gas form, with the saturation constant converted by $\ln(\mathcal R T)$ in
`equilibrate_uv` ({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_uv.h equilibrate_uv >}}) and partial pressures
$p\, x_n / x_{\mathrm g}$ in `equilibrate_tp` ({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_tp.h equilibrate_tp >}}). The same
holds for the relative humidity (@sec-ch03-relative-humidity). A non-ideal state would then be adjusted to an
ideal-gas saturation; that it would be inconsistent with this section's pressure is a hypothesis (not run).
